1:12.sourceText: ὃν ἀνέπεμψά σοι αὐτόν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὰ ἐμὰ σπλάγχνα·
1:12.targetText: whom I sent again to you—he who is my own heart,

groups.note: The sending-back verb ἀνέπεμψα is rendered I sent again by LSV; again expresses that return/re-sending prefix in this context, without an independent Greek again adverb.

Greek resumptive him plus that-is explanation, αὐτόν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν, identifies the returned Onesimus with Paul’s inward affections. LSV recasts the whole explanation as personal he who is; the accusative person and neuter explanatory formula are retained without pretending there is a separately written personal relative pronoun.

The actual Greek is plural σπλάγχνα, inward parts/tender affections, metaphorically applied to Onesimus; LSV uses singular heart. The original head is not relabeled as the different Greek καρδία heart noun.
